mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) above 600,000 units signals robust housing demand, which correlates with higher consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST exceeds 600,000 units but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.15% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary easing that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.15% for two months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates labor market tightening that accelerates wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During high consumer demand regimes (RSAFS > 390,000 million dollars), strong household spending supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS exceeds 390,000 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% annually but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0% for three consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 5.0% for three months but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals monetary tightening with economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During strong industrial expansion (INDPRO > 95.0), robust manufacturing output supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO exceeds 95.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
